pa_main_wall_5.blurb: The tallest and easiest-to-reach cliff on a pebbly conglomerate ridge in south-central Pennsylvania, set in the hills near Swatara Gap. Around twenty lines of roughly 45 to 50 feet face south, so the wall catches sun and warms up early on cool days. Most of it is crack climbing on trad gear, with a handful of bolted face lines and several top-rope setups. Grades run from easy 5.5 cracks through a solid block of 5.9 and 5.10, topping out in the 5.11 range. Pebbles can pop out of the conglomerate, so test holds and wear a helmet. A good pick for moderate trad and top-roping close to the Harrisburg area.
pa_main_wall_5.approach: From the pullout, walk east on the dirt road past the gates to a burn site, then watch on the left for a small wooden sign for Boxcar Rd. Take the first real trail heading south; it brings you to the back of the rocks.

pa_breadloaf_immediate_vicinity.blurb: A cluster of about twenty boulder problems gathered around the tall Breadloaf boulder inside the Governor Stable boulder field near Elizabethtown, in Lancaster County. The blocks are diabase, which polishes easily, so keep your shoes clean. Grades spread widely: a bunch of easy V0 and VB warm-ups, a strong middle of V3 to V5 problems, and a few much harder lines up to the low double digits. The hollow is sheltered from wind and runs warm on sunny days, which makes it a favorite for cold weather, while summer heat is a real drawback. Bring several pads, since landings vary.

pa_3_6_zero_wing.blurb: A taller crag on the northern half of the Safe Harbor cliffs, found at roughly mile 3.6 along the Enola Low Grade rail trail in Lancaster County. About twenty routes sit on two main lines of wall, mostly bolted sport with some trad and one top-rope. The range is broad: one beginner-level top-rope, then a tidy run of 5.6 to 5.9 moderates, and a solid group of 5.10s and a couple of 5.11s on the harder end. Expect the steeper, more spread-out character of the northern crags rather than the compact walls to the south, and bring a 60 m rope plus a mix of draws.

pa_danger_dam_the.blurb: A boulder area inside Philadelphia's Wissahickon Valley Park, tucked beside the Lincoln Drive bike path uphill from the Ridge Avenue end. Roughly twenty problems on Wissahickon schist, from V0 through V7, with the grades fairly evenly spread and a good number of easy to moderate lines plus a few hard ones. Many problems have extra variations, and a long traverse links much of the area. Locals rate it among the best city bouldering, and the surrounding woods feel remote despite the neighborhood. Bring pads and a spotter, and expect plenty of hikers and cyclists passing in good weather.

pa_k_hydroman_sector.blurb: The northernmost stretch of Safe Harbor South, beside the old railroad bed in Lancaster County, near the dam. About twenty routes of mostly bolted single-pitch sport, with some trad lines and top-rope options. Grades cluster at 5.9 to 5.11, with a couple of easier 5.7 and 5.8 warm-ups, so it suits climbers working through the 5.10s. Late afternoon light lingers on the wall longer than at many neighboring sectors. It is the last sector you reach on the walk in from the tunnel, so expect a bit more quiet than the busy southern walls.
pa_k_hydroman_sector.parking_note: Leave the car on Green Hill Road next to the tunnel. Room is limited, so park tightly and leave space for others to turn around.
